paragraphs: GridUnity sells software for transmission and distribution interconnection, aimed at making energy project approvals faster. It is built for the parties on both sides of an interconnection request, including ISOs, RTOs, utilities, developers and transmission owners.

The platform runs the life cycle from application intake to commissioning in one place. It is delivered as configurable software as a service, which the company says lets customers meet federal and state orders as those evolve. Near real-time data sharing among developers, utilities and regulators is offered as a way to cut disputes and speed studies. The company states compliance with NIST 800-171 and SOC 2 Type II standards.

Products are broken out for transmission, for large load and for distribution. On its own record the company cites a five-year research and development strategy focused on AI, automation and predictive analytics. It also cites $45 million in matching Department of Energy funding and GRIP award recognition. Collaboration with research institutions and government agencies is described as part of that work.

quote.text: The challenge of increasing electricity demand is making the massive interconnection backlog more problematic.
